title: Prove the long-running procedure worker contract
description:
Prove that the generic command worker can execute registered procedure commands that run for up to approximately twelve hours without introducing a separate procedure worker or dashboard-specific execution path.

Intent:
- Preserve one structured command service and one portable executor boundary.
- Support long-running optimization procedures as ordinary registered procedure.run workloads.
- Keep dashboard launch/management controls out of scope.

Required proof:
- A verified Task account context reaches procedure execution.
- Queue visibility and durable lease renewal remain valid for the full supported duration.
- ECS task protection covers active execution and is cleared after settlement.
- Cancellation and ownership loss have explicit behavior; an abandoned worker cannot silently produce an authoritative terminal result.
- Worker concurrency cannot clear task-level protection while another command in the same ECS task is active. Prefer one command per ECS task unless a simpler proven protection reference-count exists.
- Long work does not indefinitely block short queued commands; define horizontal scaling from observable queue/workload signals rather than an unexplained fixed concurrency assumption.
- Tests use accelerated clocks/fakes plus a bounded real command smoke; no twelve-hour CI test is required.
- Provider-specific ECS protection stays behind the existing portable runtime port so a Kubernetes deployment can use its own adapter.

Non-goals:
- No dashboard controls or workflow redesign.
- No second command protocol, state store, dispatcher, or Celery replacement.
- No production deployment in this sub-task.

Acceptance criteria:
- The generic worker executes a representative structured procedure.run through the real executor boundary.
- Accelerated coverage proves lease, visibility, protection, cancellation, and terminal-state behavior across the twelve-hour support window.
- Concurrency and scaling behavior are explicit, tested, and justified by the long-running/interactive workload mix.
- The result is documented as a reusable worker capability, not a dashboard-specific special case.
